extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and licensees in FCC wireless radio services; broadcast/telecom engineers; FCC attorneys and consultants
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for filing, amending, coordinating, and seeking waivers for wireless radio service applications with the FCC, including interference-protection/coordination obligations for special receiving sites and cross-border frequency coordination with Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and disclosure of TINs (Debt Collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Debt Collection Improvement Act of 1996 (DCIA), the FCC may use an applicant or licensee's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for collecting and reporting delinquent amounts to the Department of the Treasury; the Commission will not publicly disclose TINs unless authorized by law and will assign a 'public identification number' to each applicant or licensee registering a TIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public identification number will be used for agency purposes other than debt collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant email address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must specify an email address where the applicant can receive electronic correspondence, unless an exception is set forth elsewhere in the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This email will be used by the Commission to serve documents or direct correspondence; any correspondence sent to the email currently on file is deemed served. Applicants should also provide a United States Postal Service address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet zones: general obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas where it is necessary to restrict radiation to minimize possible impact on radio astronomy or other facilities highly sensitive to interference are designated as quiet zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent in this paragraph means written consent from the quiet zone, radio astronomy, research, and receiving installation entity; the section then sets out the areas involved and required procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRAO/NRRO notification for specified Green Bank/Sugar Grove area
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and licensees planning new or modified stations at permanent fixed locations within the specified bounded area must notify the Director, National Radio Astronomy Observatory (Green Bank) in writing of technical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include geographical coordinates of antenna location, antenna height, antenna directivity (if any), the channel, emission type and power. Notification may be made prior to or simultaneously with FCC application; the FCC allows 20 days for comments/objections after application is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRAO/NRRO written consent effect and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant submits written consent from NRAO (for itself or on behalf of NRRO), the FCC will process the application without awaiting the 20-day comment period; entities with written consent for services not requiring individual station authorization may begin operation prior to the end of the 20-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notification was made prior to filing, applicant must provide notice to the quiet zone entity upon actual filing, simultaneous with the filing and complying with notification content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Mountain: field strength limits
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent degradation at the Table Mountain Radio Receiving Zone, field strengths (excluding reflected signals) resulting from new assignments/modifications must not exceed specified values for frequency ranges (table listing field strength mV/m and equivalent power flux density dBW/m^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent power flux density values assume free space characteristic impedance of 376.7 ohms (120π Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Mountain: advance consultation coordination thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance consultation with Department of Commerce is recommended when applicants lack reliable data to determine whether the Table Mountain limits would be exceeded; general coordination is recommended for specified distance/power thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended coordination cases include: within 2.4 km (1.5 mi); within 4.8 km (3 mi) transmitting ≥50 W ERP in primary plane toward Table Mountain; within 16 km (10 mi) transmitting ≥1 kW ERP toward Table Mountain; within 80 km (50 mi) transmitting ≥25 kW ERP toward Table Mountain. Applicants are urged to contact the Radio Frequency Manager in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC protected field offices: avoidance of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and licensees planning new or modified stations near an FCC protected field office should consider avoiding interference with that office's monitoring activities; protected field offices are listed in § 0.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is intended to minimize interference to FCC monitoring activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected field office threshold for examination and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications (except mobile stations) that could produce a direct wave fundamental field strength >10 mV/m in the authorized bandwidth at a protected field office may be examined for interference potential; the FCC may add a condition restricting radiation toward the protected field office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination considers predicted field strength and cumulative ambient field strength effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected field office: consultation and coordination recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: If calculated field strength exceeds 10 mV/m or there is uncertainty, advance consultation with the FCC (Chief, Enforcement Bureau) is recommended; general coordination is recommended for stations within specified distances/power levels similar to Table Mountain thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination recommended: within 2.4 km; within 4.8 km with ≥50 W ERP; within 16 km with ≥1 kW ERP; within 80 km with ≥25 kW ERP. Advance coordination for >1000 MHz recommended only for facilities designated as satellite monitoring facilities in § 0.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arecibo Observatory notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees planning new stations or modifications at permanent fixed locations on Puerto Rico, Desecheo, Mona, Vieques or Culebra (or operations that may cause interference) must notify the Interference Office, Arecibo Observatory, in writing or electronically of technical parameters of the planned operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include antenna coordinates (NAD-83), antenna height, antenna directivity (if any), proposed channel and FCC Rule Part, type of emission, and effective isotropic radiated power. Carriers may use Cornell University's interference guidelines as design guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arecibo: amateur service exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arecibo notification provisions do not apply to amateur repeaters transmitting on 1.2 cm or shorter wavelength bands, and coordination provision does not apply to repeaters located 16 km or more from Arecibo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit carve-outs within the Arecibo notification paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arecibo: timing and comment period rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For services with individual station licenses, notification may be made prior to or simultaneously with FCC application filing and at least 20 days before planned operation; for services without individual station licenses, send notification at least 45 days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For services without individual licenses, the Interference Office must inform FCC within 20 days if it plans to file comments/objections. After FCC receives application or is informed, the Interference Office has 20 days for comments/objections. Written consent from the Interference Office allows FCC to process without waiting. Entities with written consent for services not requiring individual authorization may operate prior to the end of the 20-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arecibo: frequency >15 GHz exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arecibo notification provisions do not apply to operations that transmit on frequencies above 15 GHz.

rubrics_metrics.name: 420-450 MHz band: accommodation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for pulse-ranging radiolocation systems in 420-450 MHz (and spread spectrum in 420-435 MHz) along shorelines should not expect accommodation if their service area falls within specified states/portions or listed circular areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed geographic exclusions include Arizona, Florida, New Mexico; portions of CA and NV south of latitude 37°10′ N; portion of TX west of longitude 104° W; and several circular areas defined by center coordinates and radii (e.g., 322 km of 30°30′ N., 86°30′ W., etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 17.7-19.7 GHz band: exclusion and coordination areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion and coordination areas are established to minimize harmful interference to Federal earth stations in 17.7-19.7 GHz; no applications will be accepted for certain fixed-station MVPD operations if located within specified distances of Denver or Washington (20 km or 55 km for certain modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application for new station license or modification that changes frequency, power, emission, modulation, polarization, antenna height/directivity, or location in these bands must be coordinated with the Federal Government before authorization if located in listed areas (detailed latitude/longitude rectangles and radii for Denver, Washington, San Miguel, Guam). Coordinates are NAD-83.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOES (1670-1675 MHz) notification and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and licensees planning new or modified stations within specified radii of Wallops Island, Fairbanks, or Greenbelt (GOES earth station sites) must notify NOAA of the proposed operation and provide technical parameters (requested frequency, antenna coordinates, height AMSL, directivity, emission type, EIRP, antenna and transmitter make/model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wallops Island and Fairbanks must be protected at all times; Greenbelt must be protected only when active, and licensees should coordinate procedures with NOAA for active times. The NOAA GOES coordination web page provides technical parameters and points of contact. When filing with FCC, notification should be sent at same time and application must state date of NOAA notification; FCC allows 20 days for comments/objections. If NOAA objects during 20 days FCC will take appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver authority (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may waive specific rule requirements on its own motion or upon request; fees for waiver requests are set in § 1.1102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver filing procedure and required form
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for waiver of rules associated with licenses/applications in the Wireless Radio Services must be filed on FCC Form 601, 603, or 605.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must contain a complete explanation why the waiver is desired; if supporting information is already on file, the applicant may cross-reference the specific filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for granting a waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant a waiver if it is shown that (i) application of the rule to the instant case would not serve or would frustrate the underlying purpose of the rule and that a grant would be in the public interest; or (ii) unique or unusual factual circumstances make application of the rule inequitable, unduly burdensome, or contrary to the public interest, or the applicant has no reasonable alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the two alternative legal standards for waiver grants under § 1.925.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited waiver requests labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants requiring expedited processing of their waiver request must clearly caption their request with 'WAIVER—EXPEDITED ACTION REQUESTED.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver request public notice and effect of denial
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may give public notice of a waiver filing and seek comment; denial of a rule waiver request associated with an application renders that application defective unless it contains an alternative fully complying with the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is rendered defective and lacks a compliant alternative it may be dismissed without prejudice; if an alternative is provided the application will be processed using the alternative as if the waiver had not been requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing: file numbers and service codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned file numbers and service codes to facilitate processing; assignment of a file number is for administrative convenience and does not constitute a determination that the application is acceptable for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and service codes appear on Commission forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of applications: right to amend (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending applications may be amended as a matter of right if they have not been designated for hearing or listed in a public notice as accepted for filing for competitive bidding, except as provided in paragraphs (b) through (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments for auctionable services restricted to Subpart Q
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for an initial license in auctionable services may amend such applications only in accordance with Subpart Q of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to non-auction Part 101 or mutual exclusivity resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to non-auction applications that are applied for under Part 101 or that resolve mutual exclusivity may be filed at any time, subject to the requirements of § 1.945.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency requirement for modification amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to an application for modification must be consistent with, and must not conflict with, any other application for modification regarding that same station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in designated-for-hearing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to applications designated for hearing may be allowed by the presiding officer or, when proceeding is stayed or pending before the full Commission, by the Commission for good cause shown; a written petition demonstrating good cause must be submitted and served on parties of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-specific rules apply to amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to applications are also subject to the service-specific rules in applicable parts of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment effecting substantial change in beneficial ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment specifies a substantial change in beneficial ownership or control (de jure or de facto), the applicant must provide an exhibit with the amendment application containing an affirmative, factual showing as set forth in § 1.948(i)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes a documentary/exhibit requirement tied to ownership/control changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments constituting a major change treated as new application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment to an application constitutes a major change (as defined in § 1.929), the amendment shall be treated as a new application for determination of filing date, public notice, and petition to deny purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to petitioners and mutually exclusive applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to deny or informal objection has been filed, a copy of any amendment (or other filing) must be served on the petitioner; if FCC has issued public notice stating the application appears mutually exclusive with other applications, a copy of any amendment must be served on any such mutually exclusive applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada frequency coordination: that arrangement exists and covered bands
rubrics_metrics.description: By mutual agreement, the Commission has an arrangement with the Canadian Department of Communications (since May 1950) for exchange of frequency assignment information and engineering comments on proposed assignments along the Canada-US borders in certain bands above 30 MHz; the rule lists the specific MHz and GHz bands involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: frequencies excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain frequencies are not involved in the arrangement because of the nature of the services; the rule lists excluded channels (e.g., many VHF marine channels like 156.3–157.40 range and specific channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: railroad allotment plan and other exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments proposed in accordance with the railroad industry radio frequency allotment plan along the border may be excepted at the discretion of the referring agency; assignments in bands below 470 MHz may be excepted under specified conditions (prior base station assignment and similar technical characteristics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary exceptions exist if additional station characteristics are sufficiently similar to original assignment to preclude harmful interference across the border.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: geographic Line A-D areas for <470 MHz
rubrics_metrics.description: For bands below 470 MHz, the involved areas lie between Lines A and B and between Lines C and D, which are defined by detailed great circle arcs and parallels (text provides full geographic descriptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines A-D are long-form geographic definitions that delineate coordination areas between the U.S. and Canada, including Alaskan panhandle inclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: 470-1000 MHz and >1000 MHz sector/distance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For stations using bands between 470 MHz and 1000 MHz, and for terrestrial service stations using bands above 1000 MHz, involved areas are: (1) for antennas looking within a 200° sector toward the border, area within 35 miles of border; (2) for antennas looking within a 160° sector away from the border, area within 5 miles of border; (3) area within coordination distance as described in Recommendation 1A of the Final Acts of EARC, Geneva, 1963 of a receiving earth station in the other country which uses the same band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: space services and above-1 GHz coequal allocations excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed assignments in space radiocommunication services and to stations in bands allocated coequally to space and terrestrial services above 1 GHz are not treated by these arrangements; such assignments are subject to International Radio Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada coordination: 806-890 MHz agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments proposed in the frequency band 806-890 MHz shall be in accordance with the Canada-United States agreement dated April 7, 1982.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of filings: major actions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and amendments for stations in Wireless Radio Services are classified as major or minor; for all stations the following are major: (1) application for initial authorization; (2) any substantial change in ownership or control including partitioning/disaggregation requests; (3) application for renewal; (4) application/amendment requesting authorization for facility that may have a significant environmental effect as defined in § 1.1307, unless determined not to have significant effect; (5) application/amendment requiring frequency coordination pursuant to Commission rules or international treaty; (6) application/amendment requesting to add a frequency or frequency block for which the applicant is not currently authorized (excluding removing a frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories reference § 309 of the Communications Act and cross-referenced environmental provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular-specific major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: In Cellular Radiotelephone Service, additional major changes include: (1) application requesting authorization to expand the Cellular Geographic Service Area (CGSA) of an existing system; (2) application/amendment requesting that a CGSA boundary or portion be determined using an alternative method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-to-mobile/site-specific services: major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For stations licensed to provide base-to-mobile, mobile-to-base, mobile-to-mobile on a site-specific basis, major changes include increased/expanded composite interference contour (Paging/Radiotelephone/Rural Radiotelephone/800 MHz SMR), increases in service area for certain services (900 MHz SMR, 220 MHz), requests that establish a new fixed transmission path, or modifications increasing ERP, antenna height, or relocating transmitter for fixed stations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes specific enumerated service types and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLMRS and related services: examples of major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: In Private Land Mobile Radio Services, remote pickup broadcast auxiliary service, and GMRS systems licensed to non-individuals, major changes include: change in frequency or modification of channel pairs (except deletions), change in emission type, change in ERP or transmitter power, change in antenna height, change in authorized location or number of base stations/fixed/control stations (with exceptions), and change in class of a land station (e.g., multiple licensed to cooperative use, shared to unshared).

rubrics_metrics.name: Microwave, aural/television broadcast auxiliary: major action criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, multipoint-to-point communications or area-specific communications under part 101, major actions (in addition to paragraph (a)) include: any change in transmit antenna location by more than 5 seconds in latitude/longitude; any increase in frequency tolerance; any increase in bandwidth; any change in emission type; any increase in EIRP greater than 3 dB; any increase in transmit antenna height (AMSL) more than 3 meters (with exceptions); any increase in transmit antenna beamwidth (with exceptions); any change in polarization; any change in transmit antenna azimuth greater than 1 degree (with exceptions); any change which together with prior minor modifications produces cumulative effect exceeding any of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions for changes to certain MAS/DEMS remote/user units and specific path/system types where some parameters are typical or fixed per Form instructions. Paragraph (d)(3) lists systems exempt from some major criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-ground radiotelephone service: major actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Major actions include: request to relocate an existing General Aviation ground station; request for the first authorization for a new Commercial Aviation ground station at locations other than those listed in § 22.859.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial radiopositioning, Maritime and Aviation services: major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Major changes include any change in antenna azimuth, beamwidth, antenna location, emission type, increase in antenna height, increase in authorized power, or increase in emission bandwidth for stations licensed to provide certain industrial radiopositioning, Maritime and Aviation services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to stations for which frequencies are assigned on an exclusive basis, except certain listed services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime Public Coast VHF: international coordination is major
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change requiring international coordination in the Maritime Public Coast VHF (CMRS) Service is classified as major.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship stations: major actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Major actions for ship stations include requests for additional equipment, a change in ship category, a request for assignment of a Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI) number, or a request to increase the number of ships on an existing fleet license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft stations: major actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Major actions for aircraft stations include a request to increase the number of aircraft on an existing fleet license or a request to change the type of aircraft (private or air carrier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amateur licenses: major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Major changes for amateur licenses include an upgrade of an existing license or a change of call sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default classification: unlisted changes are minor
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change not specifically listed above as major is considered minor (see § 1.947(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the catch-all rule for classifying filings as minor when not enumerated as major.
